Simulate Distance-Removal Surveys from a Fitted Model

Source: R/gdistremoval.R
simulate_gdistremoval.Rd

Draw new distance and removal count histories from a fitted unmarked::gdistremoval() model, holding its coefficients and kernel scales at their estimates. Each visit uses its own detection probabilities, and the distance and removal histories of a visit describe the same simulated individuals. Use the replicates to study how the model behaves or to build conditional predictive checks.

Usage

simulate_gdistremoval(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  newdata = NULL,
  kernel_inputs = NULL,
  join_by = NULL,
  include_fixed = FALSE,
  re.form = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted unmarkedFitGDR model, or a multiScaleR fit from multiScale_optim() that contains one.

nsim

Positive whole number of replicate frames. Default 1.

newdata

An unmarkedFrameGDR describing the prediction sites, their visits, covariates, and removal interval durations. The default NULL uses the fitted frame. For new sites, supply response matrices of zeros with the same layout. Distance breaks and their units must match the fitted survey footprint. Removal durations must be positive integers and may differ from the fitted ones, so you can predict a longer or shorter count.

kernel_inputs

Optional kernel_prep() output for the prediction sites. With a multiScaleR fit and explicit newdata, the spatial site covariates are rebuilt at the fitted scales with the training normalization, as in prepare_unmarked_data(). Without it, the covariates in newdata are used as they are.

join_by

Data frame of prediction-site keys, required with kernel_inputs. See prepare_unmarked_data().

include_fixed

Logical. Default FALSE. With kernel_inputs, set TRUE to rebuild and check fixed-radius metrics in the model.

re.form

Random-effect policy passed to unmarked::predict(). The default NULL uses the fitted group effects. NA sets group deviations to zero, for example at sites in unsampled groups. Neither averages over the random-effect distribution.

Value

A list of nsim unmarkedFrameGDR objects with the covariates and protocol of the prediction frame and simulated counts. A visit with a missing distance or removal history in the frame stays missing in both. The prediction_contract attribute records that coefficients and scales are fixed and that latent abundance and observation noise are simulated.

Details

This function is experimental. Its arguments and results may change in a later release without a deprecation period.

Latent abundance is drawn once per site and shared by its visits: Poisson for "P", negative binomial with the fitted size for "NB", and a structural zero with the fitted probability followed by a Poisson draw for "ZIP". The number counted at each visit is binomial with the detection probability from predict_gdistremoval(). That total is then split independently among the distance bins and among the removal intervals with the fitted cell probabilities.

Call set.seed() first for reproducible draws. Group effects follow re.form; new group effects are not drawn. These conditional replicates alone are not a calibrated bootstrap of random-effect variances, selected scales, or model selection, which would need the whole fitting and sampling process repeated.

unmarked::simulate() is not used. In unmarked 1.5.2 it applies the first visit's distance parameter to every visit and back-transforms the zero-inflation parameter with exp(), whereas the likelihood uses plogis().

See also

predict_gdistremoval(), sim_dat_gdr()

Examples

y <- matrix(c(2, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 3, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
frame <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR(y, y, dist.breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 100),
  unitsIn = "m")
model <- unmarked::gdistremoval(data = frame, K = 25, se = FALSE)
set.seed(14)
replicate <- simulate_gdistremoval(model)[[1]]
# Both histories count the same simulated individuals
rowSums(replicate@yDistance) == rowSums(replicate@yRemoval)
#> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE
